## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Viravapupphiyattheraapadāna* is a verse narrative located in the Therāpadāna section of the Pali canon. Representing the late canonical Apadāna genre, it records the past devotional deeds and spiritual attainment of the elder Viravapupphiya. The text has been recorded with translations available in five languages.

No cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections are reported [DharmaNexus]. Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus reveals extensive formulaic overlap with other verse biographies in the Therāpadāna, particularly those concerning flower offerings [DharmaNexus]. Its closest textual alignments include the *Mandāravapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 363, segments §1.4–5.1 matching §3.1–6.1), the *Nigguṇḍipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 207, segments §1.3–5.1 matching §1.3–6.1), the *Ticampakapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 256, segments §2.1–5.1 matching §3.1–6.1), and both *Saḷalapupphiyattheraapadāna* texts (Tha-Ap 270 and Tha-Ap 372) [DharmaNexus]. Additional shared phrasing is found in other floral apadānas as well as the first part of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
